scenes.text: Why do a few extra miles an hour matter so much to a wind turbine? One number: three.
Power in moving air rises with the cube of wind speed. Double the wind, and the power is multiplied by eight.
But too much wind is dangerous. The Energy Department says controllers typically shut turbines off once winds exceed 55 to 65 miles an hour.
That's why the windiest day can be a zero day. The full video is on The Hidden Grid.
